## Scope and evidence

This covers the private D187 PG18.6 bottle input seam, not a public macOS compatibility claim or final installer acceptance. EI-25325563417284586 owns the provider repair; WI-10007134 owns independent rig verification. The original Intel initdb selected Homebrew's share directory despite a postgres.bki present in the inventoried native input. Local regression tests and static input preparation do not substitute for native runtime qualification.

## Why dylib normalization was insufficient

Upstream PostgreSQL src/port/path.c make_relative_path derives share and package-library paths from PGBINDIR. It relocates only when the compiled bin-directory tail matches the executable's real directory. The PG18.6 bottles compile PGBINDIR as a Homebrew Cellar/version/bin path; the maintained npm platform package executes native/bin. Therefore stock PG falls back to compiled Homebrew PGSHAREDIR/PKGLIBDIR. src/common/exec.c canonicalizes executable symlinks before this calculation. Changing only Mach-O load commands does not change these constants. Supplying -L to a test alone leaves runtime plpgsql, encoding conversions and vector library resolution unproved.

## Repair and verification procedure

1. Preserve failed banks, upstream archives and exact rig output. Never modify an immutable failed bank, install host Homebrew data to mask the problem, or restart the same failed input.
2. Use the existing darwin-native-inputs.py assembler, not a separate provider. On the newly copied PG tree it replaces the pinned exact NUL-bounded compiled path strings with shorter NUL-padded constants sharing one synthetic prefix. That preserves binary offsets and makes bin, share/postgresql and lib/postgresql resolve relative to the maintained native/bin exports. Missing or ambiguous core constants fail before any replacement is written. LLVM load-command normalization and rcodesign still run afterward.
3. Bind postgresqlPathRelocation to the FINAL emitted population after dependency closure and signing. Closure can copy normalized libpq/libecpg under short sonames; a pre-closure inventory omits those copies. The first real repair preparation demonstrated this fail-closed mismatch (41 recorded paths, 43 emitted). collect_postgres_paths now measures final aliases; verify rejects absent/forged records, old compiled paths and missing BKI/plpgsql inputs.
4. Run the registered desktop Node native-ABI and embedded-PG-lock suites through the documented package runner with monorepo-host-preflight. The tests cover both architectures, length preservation, invalid constants/no-write behavior, actual assembler alias copying, and stale final inventory rejection. Freeze exactly those tested helper bytes and confirm equality to the committed helper/test files before producing a qualification packet.
5. Assemble into a fresh bank from retained pinned upstream inputs. Validate the whole actual Mach-O closure, target and measured minimum OS; obtain a new exact-input security verdict and bind it through bind-security. Preserve full source/tool/manifest hashes.
6. Hand the new immutable packet to the registered rig owner. Native initdb/start/query/stop, plpgsql/conversion and vector loading, plus CLI protocols, are separate runtime proof. Only the resulting source-bound native receipt can qualify the input for the producer's require-runtime gate. Candidate construction, final artifact audits and independent GO/publication remain separate.

## Detector failure

The original static guard measured architecture, minimum OS and dylib links but omitted PG compiled data/library paths. The original relocation unit fixture also omitted dependency-closure-created aliases. Guards must inspect both this path class and the final transformed artifact population, not only the first copy. No runtime acceptance is implied by an inventory or local test pass.
